$comment: The form of the list of what holds each rule, as scripts/holders.mjs merges the entries of scripts/holders/ (a file for each rule: "rule", and its "holder", "behind" and "number") into { holders, behind, numbers }, each keyed by the rule; its header says what each part means. The keys' form, "#N" or "#N.P" beside the numbers up to the last numbered item, is archive.mjs's KEY and LAST_NUMBERED, which the holders check's own test holds this schema to. What a schema cannot say stays with the script: that a key names a rule as it stands, that a check named is there, a holder's form (its parts are read there), an item that is not in the archive, a number's form, which outcomes.mjs builds from its lists, and each entry's file and its name. Each rule's mend is what a failure of it says (scripts/schemas.mjs).
title: scripts/holders/
mend: write each rule's entry as a file of scripts/holders/: {"rule": its file and lead, "holder": ..., "behind": [...], "number": "..."}, each but "rule" only where the rule has one

holders.mend: write each rule's "holder" in its entry, whose "rule" is its file and lead ("floor/security.md: 1. Nothing secret in the repository")

additionalProperties.mend: write the rule's holder as "check: <its script, test, workflow or GitHub's setting>", "audit" or "describes", each with ", in part" where it holds only some of the rule, or a list of them

items.mend: write each holder as "check: <its script, test, workflow or GitHub's setting>", "audit" or "describes", each with ", in part" where it holds only some of the rule

behind.mend: write each rule's "behind" in its entry, whose "rule" is its file and lead, or a rule file alone, as the list of the keys of the items behind it

additionalProperties.mend: write it as a list of the keys of the items behind the rule, such as [134, "#744"]

items.mend: write an item's key as the archive keys it: its number up to 262 (a number, not a string), or "#N" for the issue that carries the owner's word, or "#N.P" for one point of it (#744)

numbers.mend: write each rule's "number" in its entry, whose "rule" is its file and lead, as the number the rule names

additionalProperties.mend: write "<findings | check fires | correction: <kind>>; outcome: <asked | fast | readable | usable | robust>", the count the rule is meant to lower and the outcome it stands for, with "; rare harm" at its end where the rule guards against rare and severe harm
